Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a widened, lobulated anterior mediastinal silhouette (confirmed by the lateral view showing retrosternal opacity) accompanied by blunting of both costophrenic angles, indicating bilateral pleural effusions. This combination is most consistent with an aggressive anterior mediastinal mass (such as lymphoma or thymoma) with possible vascular or lymphatic invasion leading to effusions, whereas the other options describe posterior locations or lack the associated effusions seen here.
